proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity of an obligation to compel or bind its bearer toward action or forbearance. It is internally grounded in the obligation itself (the bearer), not contingent on external recognition in any particular instance — it is a stable capacity that may or may not be realized in a given process of compliance or enforcement. BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) captures this: a disposition inheres in its bearer and is grounded in the bearer's intrinsic properties, and is realized in processes. Role (BFO_0000023) is less apt because normative force is not externally conferred by social context but is a structural feature of the obligation-type. Quality (BFO_0000019) is less apt because normative force is not a static measurable property but an active capacity. Realizable entity (BFO_0000017) is the broader class; Disposition is the correct subtype. The normative force of an obligation thus inheres in the obligation (which is a specifically dependent continuant/role inhering in a person) and is realized in processes of compliance, enforcement, or acknowledgment.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is a subclass of Disposition because it is an internally grounded capacity of its bearer (the obligation) to be realized in processes such as compliance, enforcement, or legal adjudication.

Candidate relation only: normative force inheres in (RO_0000052) instances of LegalObligation. This would be expressed as a domain restriction. Flagged for user confirmation since it constrains the bearer to LegalObligation specifically, whereas normative force might attach to moral obligations as well.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce be restricted to inhere only in LegalObligation instances, or should it be applicable to moral and other normative obligations as well? This affects whether we add a domain restriction to LegalObligation.

Is 'normative force' intended as a property of an individual obligation token (an individual disposition inhering in a specific obligation instance) or as a class-level characterization? If the former, should we also mint an individual like 'NormativeForceOfContractualObligation'?

Should NormativeForce be realized specifically in processes like working:BehavioralLegalManifestation (compliance) or working:ActOfAcknowledgment (enforcement)? If so, we can add BFO_0000054 (realized in) relations pointing to those process classes.

Is there a distinction intended between normative force as a disposition (capacity to bind) and normative force as a quality (degree of bindingness, e.g., peremptory vs. default norms)? If the latter dimension is important, a parallel Quality subclass may also be warranted.
proposal.rationale_summary: The normative force of an obligation is best captured as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) because it is a capacity that inheres in the obligation itself — grounded in the obligation's structural and social constitution — and is realized when the obligated party complies, when enforcement occurs, or when the obligation is acknowledged. Disposition is preferred over Role (BFO_0000023) because normative force is not externally conferred in the way a social role is; it arises from the internal character of the norm. It is preferred over Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is an active, realizable capacity rather than a static measurable attribute. The existing class working:LegalObligation (typed as BFO_0000023 Role and BFO_0000020 SDC) is the natural bearer class for NormativeForce instances. The class working:NormativeForce is minted as a new subclass of BFO_0000016, with open questions raised about bearer scope and realization targets before committing relations.
